input: Refinance my student loans for a lower rate

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they want to refinance federal loans, private loans, or both changes the strategy entirely — refinancing federal loans means losing income-driven repayment and forgiveness protections.
Their credit score and income level are the primary factors lenders use to determine eligibility and rate offers, so knowing these shapes which lenders to target.
Whether a co-signer is available or being considered significantly affects the rates and lenders they can qualify for.
Knowing the current loan balance and interest rate tells us how much room there is to improve and which lenders offer competitive alternatives.
The user may prioritize a lower monthly payment (longer term) vs. less total interest paid (shorter term) — these lead to very different refinancing targets.
Whether they are currently employed, in a grace period, or struggling with payments affects urgency and which refinancing programs are accessible.
Knowing what 'done well' means — a specific rate target, a monthly savings amount, or simply getting approved — determines when the task is complete.

gold.taskTitle: Refinance Student Loans for a Lower Interest Rate
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to refinance their existing student loans to secure a lower interest rate, reducing their monthly payments or total repayment cost.

questions.title: Are your loans federal, private, or a mix?
questions.description: Identifies whether the user has federal loans (which carry forgiveness/repayment protections that are lost upon refinancing), private loans, or both — this is the single biggest factor in shaping the plan.

questions.title: What is your current total balance and interest rate?
questions.description: Knowing the existing loan amount and rate helps quantify the potential savings and identifies how aggressively to shop for lenders.

questions.title: What is your approximate credit score right now?
questions.description: Credit score is the primary eligibility and rate-determination factor for private refinancing lenders, so this narrows down realistic options.

questions.title: Are you currently employed with a steady income?
questions.description: Employment status and income stability affect lender eligibility requirements and the urgency of the refinancing decision.

questions.title: Do you have or plan to use a co-signer?
questions.description: A creditworthy co-signer can unlock better rates and more lender options, so this meaningfully changes which paths are available.

questions.title: Do you want a lower monthly payment or less total interest paid?
questions.description: This preference determines the target loan term — a longer term lowers monthly payments but increases total interest, while a shorter term does the opposite.

questions.title: What rate or monthly savings would make this feel successful?
questions.description: Defines a concrete finish line — whether that is a specific APV target, a dollar amount saved per month, or simply getting approved with any improvement.
